quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You cannot cross a single broken white or yellow line:

options.text: When it would interfere with traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do so safely without interfering with traffic.

questions.question: To make sure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You must yield for emergency vehicles:

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic signals, yield to a vehicle approaching from the right.

questions.question: Orange signs are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone signs.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange, diamond-shaped, and have black letters or symbols. They warn drivers that people are working on or near the highway.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. Move it out of traffic if possible. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Help stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency vehicles.

questions.question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at:
questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks. They show where drivers must stop.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane, one-way street or highway, start from:
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: To turn left from multilane streets and highways, start from the left lane.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to oncoming traffic. Always yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers already in the intersection.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 25 mph.
questions.explanation: Unless posted otherwise, do not drive faster than 25 mph in school zones. Always be careful when driving near schools.

questions.question: You have an upsetting incident at work that made you angry. When you get to your car, you should:

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
Stop at a bar and have drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset, angry, or distracted by emotions, wait before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that traffic may enter from a side road ahead.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs order drivers to obey specific rules. You can be punished if you do not follow them.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: You must turn left or right.
You are approaching a T intersection.
Your road is crossing a divided highway.
You are on an overpass above a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your road is crossing a divided highway.
questions.explanation: This sign means your road crosses a divided highway. A divided highway has two one-way roads separated by a median or guard rail.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a pedestrian crossing ahead. Watch for people in the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: A seat belt should be adjusted so that it:

options.text: Is snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
Keeps the seat belt buzzer or light from working.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen.
questions.explanation: The lap belt should be snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen. The shoulder belt should fit comfortably so you can fit your fist between the belt and your chest.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that a stop sign is ahead. Be ready to stop completely before going forward.

questions.question: When there is a car coming at you on the left and a bicyclist on the right, you should:

options.text: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: When you face more than one hazard, handle one at a time. Do not try to get past both the car and bike at once. Let the oncoming car pass, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: A five-ounce glass of wine has the same amount of alcohol as:
questions.correctAnswerText: One 12-ounce can of beer.
questions.explanation: Most beer, wine, and liquor have about the same amount of alcohol. A five-ounce glass of wine, a 12-ounce can of beer, and 1.5 ounces of hard liquor all contain roughly the same alcohol. The type of drink does not matter—the same amount of alcohol will impair your driving the same way.

questions.question: Unless posted differently, the speed limit in suburban residential areas is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph.
questions.explanation: Unless posted differently, the speed limit in suburban residential areas is 35 mph. Follow any posted speed limit signs that show a different speed.

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right first, then left, then right again.
Look left first, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left first, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: At a stop sign, look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to check for any vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: You must travel at the speed indicated.
The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum legal speed on the roadway is 55 mph.
questions.explanation: This is a speed limit sign. It shows the fastest speed you can legally drive on this road. In bad weather or poor conditions, you may need to drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, you must:

options.text: Lock the ignition and remove the key.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: When you leave your vehicle, you must turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way if needed.
questions.explanation: This triangular sign means yield. Slow down as you approach the intersection and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, and pedestrians pass before you proceed.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, turn your steering wheel:

options.text: To keep the front wheels straight.
In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the vehicle to go.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, turn the wheel in the direction you want to go. Once the vehicle straightens out, turn the wheel the other way.

questions.question: This sign indicates that:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of these choices
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your ability to drive. This includes illegal drugs, prescription medicines, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is illegal.

questions.question: When a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System loses traction on a slippery road, drivers should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal.
Press and hold the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle loses traction on a slippery road and has ABS, press hard on the brake pedal, hold it, and steer to safety. The ABS automatically pumps the brakes faster than you can. Releasing pressure or pumping the brakes will turn off the ABS.

questions.question: When may you proceed through an intersection with a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?

options.text: After slowing down to verify that there is no cross traffic
After coming to a complete stop and verifying that it is safe to proceed
After you have stopped at least 20 feet before the intersection
After slowing down to a speed of 10 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: After coming to a complete stop and verifying that it is safe to proceed
questions.explanation: Stop before the stop line or crosswalk at any stop sign. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection. Proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers maintaining a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for the conditions. Always drive at or below the speed limit and slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: You must signal before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb because:

options.text: It is only needed if other traffic is near.
It is a good habit and is required by law.
It is only needed during the move, not before.
It is not needed if you move slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a good habit and is required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions well before turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: When a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what other drivers are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow the normal traffic laws as if construction is not happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the flagger's directions.
questions.explanation: Be ready to slow down and be careful when a sign, flagger, or police officer tells you to. Not doing so is illegal and dangerous to construction workers.

questions.question: If you drive with a suspended license and cause an accident that injures someone, you may:

options.text: Pay a fine, have your license suspended longer, and go to jail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pay a fine, have your license suspended longer, and go to jail.
questions.explanation: Driving with a suspended license is illegal. You will have to pay a fine, spend up to 45 days in jail, and get a longer license suspension.

questions.question: When driving at night and another vehicle is coming toward you, your headlights should be:

options.text: Off, with only parking lights on.
On either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: On low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when meeting or following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone safe on the road.

questions.question: A speed limit is:

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road in bad conditions.
The highest or lowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
The suggested speed on a road in good conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road in good conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but driving faster is illegal. Slow down for school zones, work zones, and bad weather. If conditions make the speed unsafe, drive slower than the posted limit.

questions.question: At a multilane intersection, you are waiting to turn left but opposing traffic blocks your view. You should:

options.text: Speed up as soon as the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for a driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and you can safely complete the turn.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, it is safest to:

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when some drivers go much faster or slower than others. Drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but stay within the speed limit.

questions.question: When you are behind a transit bus that is signaling to enter a traffic lane, you should:

options.text: Pass the bus quickly before it moves.
Let the bus enter the traffic lane.
Expect the bus to wait for you.
You can choose to let it in or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the bus enter the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: You must yield the right-of-way to a transit bus that is signaling to enter your lane. Slow down or change lanes to help the bus merge safely.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, turn on your headlights. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of oncoming traffic or within 500 feet of traffic ahead of you. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: A solid white line on the right edge of the highway angles toward the left. What does this mean?

options.text: You are approaching a construction area.
You must turn left just ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will become narrower.
questions.explanation: A solid line on the side of the road marks the edge and the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder. If the edge line angles toward the center of the road, the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, what should you do?

options.text: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to your lane when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, you must return to the right side when there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: A driver under 21 with a probationary license:

options.text: Can use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
Cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
Should not wear a seat belt while driving.
Can use a handheld cell phone while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.
questions.explanation: Drivers with probationary licenses must follow certain rules. They cannot use a handheld or hands-free cell phone and must wear a seat belt. Drivers under 21 cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.question: Why should you be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than cars.
They do not have rearview mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: Many crashes with motorcycles, bicycles, and pedestrians happen because drivers did not see them. These are smaller and harder to spot because they are less noticeable in traffic. To prevent crashes, always watch for motorcycles, bikes, and pedestrians.

questions.question: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Keep the rear tires against the curb.
Keep the front tires pointing straight.
Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
Turn your steering wheel toward the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill on a curbed street, set your parking brake and turn your steering wheel away from the curb. If your vehicle rolls, it will roll into the curb and stop.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder for an emergency. Change lanes as little as possible. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Stay centered in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another vehicle is heading straight at you, first honk your horn to get their attention. If they do not move, steer to the right to escape. Do not swerve left because they may correct at the last second and you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the impact.

questions.question: It is best to keep a space cushion:

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic signal means that a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light will appear soon.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
You see in your rearview mirror.
You see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located on the sides and behind your vehicle.
